assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Regressed against S&P 500 on monthly total returns to 2026-09-17, over 72 paired observations. The proxy and the window are both judgements and both change the answer, which is why this is a proposal rather than an input.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Flagging a model mismatch: EV/EBITDA is not a meaningful bank metric, since interest expense ($828m in Q2 2026) is operating cost, not financing, and debt belongs in the capital base. 7.0x is my mapping of a mid-cycle pre-tax pre-provision earnings multiple, cross-checked against residual income: ROE 9.42% (filings-derived), g=3%, CoE ~10.5% implies ~0.85x book and ~9x net income; on ROTCE 16.5% it implies ~1.8x tangible book. The Gordon/residual-income terminal value is the better estimate here and should govern; treat this multiple as a convention-mapped placeholder, not an independent view. Consistency note: 7x is not a high multiple, but paired with 3% it reflects a sub-CoE ROE, not a contradiction.

assumptions.name: payout_ratio
assumptions.justification: The mean of dividends paid over net income across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.3120, 0.3936, 0.3167, 0.3458, 0.3153.

assumptions.name: return_on_equity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net income over equity across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.1038, 0.0787, 0.1017, 0.0892, 0.0977.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 5% on 2026-09-15, as published by 2026-09-17 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.05.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a cost of equity I assume near 10-11% (5.0% derived risk-free rate plus a regional-bank equity premium), so the spread is ~7-8 points. 3% sits at long-run nominal GDP: a deposit-funded regional franchise tied to New England/Mid-Atlantic activity grows with nominal output, not above it. I did not use the filings-implied retention growth (ROE 9.42% x (1-0.3367) = ~6.3%), which is a near-term reinvestment rate and exceeds this platform's 4% cap. Lower it toward 2-2.5% if deposit-beta pressure (56% cumulative) and fintech entry are judged to erode share; raise it only if the 5% risk-free rate is read as a permanently higher inflation regime.

outstanding.name: equity_risk_premium
outstanding.reason: The equity risk premium is a judgement with no series behind it, and no role in this platform proposes one. Enter the premium you are using and cite where it comes from — or set a standing premium in settings, and every run will propose it for you to confirm.
